scope: HR employee self-service and admin journeys in the current working tree (including uncommitted changes): Today/clock, history/day, requests/corrections, profile, holidays, employee linking/setup, review, periods, settings/access and shortcut customization. Sources: src/features/hr, src/app/[locale]/(desktop)/hr, convex/hr, src/components/providers/HrAccessProvider.tsx. Discovery only; no app source, tests, config or translations changed.

findings.title: Linking an account or supervisor in Employees looks complete but grants no HR access, and nothing tells the admin
findings.user: HR administrator setting up an employee; the linked employee; the assigned supervisor
findings.trigger: HR admin opens Employees > Add employee, selects a member under Linked account and another member under Supervisor, then saves. Neither member holds HR_EMPLOYEE / HR_SUPERVISOR. A newly invited member, or one with only a planner role, has neither.
findings.expected: Setup either gives the linked member self-service access and the supervisor review access, or the Employees form/list clearly says that the role still has to be granted in Settings > HR access (ideally with a direct action).
findings.actual: The save succeeds and the list shows the account as linked. The employee gets 'You do not have access to this page / Ask your organization's HR administrator for access' on every HR page. The supervisor cannot open Review. Member options contain only userId/displayName, so the form cannot warn. The admin must find the separate Settings > HR access checkbox on their own.
findings.cause: Account/supervisor linkage (hrEmployees.userId/supervisorUserId) and HR roles (membershipRoles) are independent. saveEmployee never grants or checks a role, memberOptions does not return role/access state, and the form hint only says that an account is needed to clock in. The demo seed grants HR_EMPLOYEE separately, which hides the gap in fixtures.
findings.evidence: Probe hr-setup.probe.ts uses real registered convex-test handlers. saveEmployee writes; then access.current, self.today and the supervisor's review.queue all return ok:false; memberOptionKeys=[displayName,userId]. The control passes once setMemberAccess grants HR_EMPLOYEE. UI consequences are source-traced.
findings.evidenceLevel: backend handler probe (convex-test) + source-traced UI; not browser-verified
findings.novelty: new — no earlier report covers link-without-role. Daily KIRO-04 concerns cross-site role revocation, not this setup gap.
findings.recommendation: Product decision: either grant HR_EMPLOYEE on link and HR_SUPERVISOR on supervisor assignment (preferred if policy allows), or add an access field to memberOptions/listEmployees and show an inline warning with a 'Grant self-service' action. Keep server authorization unchanged.
findings.testNeeded: Integration: link + supervisor assignment followed by access.current/review.queue for those users. Rendered: Employees form/list shows missing-access state for a linked member without the role.

findings.title: Certify/Return confirmation is never shown, and after Return the reviewer is shown an 'Account for this day' form or 'Nothing to decide'
findings.trigger: Review > open a day with a pending correction > Return > enter reason > Confirm return (also Certify, and Account-for-this-day submit). With live Convex data the decided state arrives before the mutation promise resolves.
findings.expected: A visible, announced confirmation such as 'Returned to Somchai', retained until the reviewer moves on. Any next action should be clearly separate from the completed return.
findings.actual: The decision component unmounts when the query drops pendingCorrectionId, so the 'Returned'/'Certified' status is lost. If the employee's own day was complete, the panel says 'Nothing on this day needs a decision.' and the desktop list shows 'The open day is not in this list's range, site or tab.' For a missing clock-out, 'Account for this day' appears immediately, as if the return still needs another action. Disposition success is also lost because its key includes the revision.
findings.cause: Write feedback lives inside CorrectionDecision/DispositionForm. Rendering of those components depends on live state that the successful write changes (pending correction; revision key). Convex resolves a successful mutation only after the reflecting query transition, so the owner publishes SAVED to an unmounted form. The existing test passes because its query never changes.
findings.evidence: hr-ui.probe.tsx renders production ReviewDetail with a reactive query store. Control (static query): 'Returned' shown. Live update on a complete day: statuses=['Nothing on this day needs a decision.'], no 'Returned'. Live update on a missing clock-out: no status; 'Account for this day' visible.
findings.evidenceLevel: rendered-component probe + Convex client source; not browser-verified
findings.novelty: new; differs from SOL-01, which concerns erased drafts, not lost completion feedback
findings.recommendation: Lift the last decision receipt to ReviewDetail (keyed by employee/date) and render it above the next state, for example 'Returned to employee · reason'. Optionally offer 'Next open day'. For a returned day, explain that the employee can resubmit before offering disposition.
findings.testNeeded: Rendered ReviewDetail with a store that publishes the post-decision detail before resolving: Return on READY and MISSING_END days, Certify, and Dispose each show a persistent role=status confirmation.

findings.title: Opening a day from History (or a request from Requests) and pressing Back resets the chosen month, filter and page
findings.user: Employee reviewing earlier attendance or request status
findings.trigger: History > choose September (and optionally the 'Needs review' filter) > open a day > Back. Or: Requests > status filter / page 3 > open a request > Back.
findings.expected: Back restores the view the employee left, including the month/range, status filter and page.
findings.actual: History remounts on the current month and All. Requests remounts on page 1 and All. The employee must choose the range or page again after every day/request check.
findings.cause: Range, filter, status and cursors are component state, not URL state. cacheComponents is disabled, so App Router unmounts the previous route, unlike the Activity behaviour in node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/preserving-ui-state.md. Review and Period already use URL-backed state for comparable context.
findings.evidence: hr-ui.probe.tsx: after choosing September the query is from=2026-09-01; window.location.search stays empty; after the remount, month=2026-10 and the query is from 2026-10-01. Requests is source-traced.
findings.evidenceLevel: rendered-component remount probe + Next config/docs source; Requests source-traced; not browser-verified
findings.confidence: high for the mechanism; the browser Back path should still be confirmed by the parent
findings.novelty: new; frontend-consistency A07 covers Requests paging presentation, not Back restoration
findings.recommendation: Store History month/from/to/filter and Requests status/cursor stack in the query string (useUrlBackedState plus replace updates), so Day/Request Back restores them. Update the back-navigation inventory for the changed state.
findings.testNeeded: Caller tests: choose month/filter > open Day > native Back > same month/filter and query args. Requests: status/page > detail > Back > same page. Also cover direct entry and locale switch.

findings.title: Resubmitting a returned correction starts from the original punch with an empty reason; the reviewer's reason appears only below the form
findings.trigger: Today or Requests > returned request > Open day. The form is titled 'Resubmit the returned request'.
findings.expected: The reviewer's return reason appears at or above the form. The form starts from the returned proposal and reason, so the employee changes only what was asked.
findings.actual: Times prefill from the original events (08:29 instead of the proposed 07:45), and the reason is empty. The return reason appears only in the Requests log after the form and the events panel, which is far below on mobile.
findings.cause: CorrectionForm initial state is the same for new and returned requests. DayDetailView renders children before the events and requests logs.
findings.evidence: hr-resubmit.probe.tsx renders production DayScreen: formStart=08:29, formReason='', and the return reason is after the form.
findings.confidence: high for behaviour; medium that prefilling the earlier proposal is the intended product rule
findings.recommendation: When returnedId is set, show a Notice with the latest RETURNED reason and reviewer above the fields. Optionally seed times/reason from the returned proposal. Keep the original-retention semantics for untouched sides.
findings.testNeeded: Rendered DayScreen with a returned correction: the reason is above/inside the form, and initial values follow the chosen product rule.

findings.title: Saving an employee closes the editor with no confirmation
findings.trigger: Employees > Add employee (or Edit) > Save employee succeeds.
findings.expected: A visible saved state, for example 'EMP-101 saved', ideally with any follow-up such as the missing HR access in K-UX-HR-01.
findings.actual: On SAVED, onDone closes the form immediately (flushSync unmount + Back/replace). WriteFeedback's 'Saved' is never rendered. The admin has to scan the list for the new or changed row; other HR writes show a saved state.
findings.cause: Completion is modelled as editor closure only; no list-level receipt exists.
findings.evidence: Source-traced. Existing EmployeesNavigation tests assert closure and history ownership, not confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Pass the saved code/name to the list and render a dismissible role=status Notice after closing, without adding a Back entry.
findings.testNeeded: Rendered Employees save → editor closes → a status names the saved employee; the next Back is unchanged.

limitations: No browser automation and no app server; the parent owns T3 browser verification. K-UX-HR-02/03 browser reproduction is still pending.
UI probes replace Convex with an in-memory reactive store. The mutation-before-query ordering is taken from the Convex client source (request_manager.js:100), not observed on a live deployment.
The backend probe uses convex-test with registered handlers and fixture roles, not Clerk or a deployed backend.
Mobile layout, keyboard focus order, screen-reader output and contrast were reviewed only by reading source; no viewport or assistive-technology run.
Requests filter/page loss, employee-save feedback and sidebar visibility for role-less linked members are source-traced only.
Line numbers refer to the working tree on 2026-10-15; the tree has many concurrent uncommitted changes.
